name: Waiter Curl
research: One upright dumbbell (handle vertical, axis +z) on db_L; the right hand sits beside it with no prop, mirror-symmetric arm angles (fore_world is world and not mirrored, so R is written with x flipped). Fists at x = +-0.045 (torso frame). 12 Nov 2026 fix: (1) the pipeline built the dumbbell's frame from its handle axis and the torso's up line; for an upright dumbbell those are the same line, so the frame was rounding noise and the dumbbell rendered tilted/flat (rig.frame_from now falls back to a fixed perpendicular). (2) prop_offset [-0.045, 0, -0.035] moves the dumbbell to the midline, between the two fists, and down so its top plate's inner face (0.082 above the dumbbell centre) sits ~5 mm above the fists' top (fist ~0.09 tall, +-0.045 about the grip centre): both hands sit under the top head, the handle hangs between them. Plates r 0.088 at fist y ~-0.20 clear the thigh front (~-0.08) by 3 cm in the start. START: elev 8 plane 60, forearm world (-0.563,-0.429,-0.709), elbow ~43 deg, fist ~world (0.045,-0.20,0.93). END: elev 12 plane 70, forearm (-0.586,-0.686,0.435), elbow ~110 deg, fist ~(0.045,-0.30,1.32). Known limit: the rig's hands are closed fists, so 'palms cupped under the plate' is drawn as two fists under the plate; the wrist bends back ~60 deg in the start (a real waiter curl does too). Facts: research/waiter_curl.json.
